title: Idolatry as the chief crime containing all others
english: Idolatry is the chief crime of the human race, the supreme guilt of the age, the whole cause of judgment. For even if each offense keeps its own form, even if each is destined for judgment under its own name, it is still blotted out under the crime of idolatry. Set aside the labels and look at the deeds. The idolater is also a murderer. Whom has he killed? If he does anything for the ambition of praise, it is not a stranger or an enemy, but himself. By what plots? By his own error. With what weapon? By offending God. With how many blows? As many as his acts of idolatry. Whoever denies that the idolater has perished will also deny that the idolater has committed murder. Likewise you may recognize adultery and fornication in the same person; for whoever serves false gods is without doubt an adulterer against truth, because every falsehood is adultery. So too he is plunged into fornication. For who cooperates with unclean spirits without walking about defiled and fornicated? Indeed the holy Scriptures use the word fornication to reproach idolatry. The nature of fraud, I think, is this: if someone seizes another's property or denies what he owes to another, and certainly fraud committed against a human being bears the name of the greatest crime. But idolatry commits fraud against God, denying Him His honors and conferring them on others, so that it joins insult to fraud. And if fraud, fornication, and adultery all bring death, then in these respects idolatry is equally not freed from the guilt of murder. After such crimes, so deadly, so devouring of salvation, the rest also, each in its own way and separately arranged, represent their own condition in idolatry. In it are the desires of the age. For what solemnity of idolatry is without the ambition of dress and adornment? In it are wantonness and drunkenness, since for the most part they are frequented for the sake of food and belly and lust. In it is injustice. For what is more unjust than that which does not know the Father of justice? In it also is vanity, since its whole reason is vain. In it is falsehood, since its whole substance is false. So it happens that all things are found in idolatry, and idolatry is found in all things. But also in another way: since all offenses savor of opposition to God, and nothing that savors of opposition to God is not assigned to demons and unclean spirits, to whom idols are enslaved, without doubt whoever sins commits idolatry. For he does what belongs to the servants of idols.
orientation: Tertullian opens his treatise by defining idolatry as the principal crime of the human race and arguing that it contains within itself every other major sin.

title: Idolatry's breadth must be recognized, not narrowed
english: But let all the names of crimes go off to the particular acts that belong to them, and let idolatry remain in what it itself is. A name so hostile to God is enough for it, and so rich a substance of crime, which stretches out so many branches and spreads so many veins, that from this especially material should be taken for how many ways the breadth of idolatry must be guarded against by us, since in many ways it overturns the servants of God, not only when it is unknown but even when it is ignored.

Most people think idolatry is to be understood only in these ways: if someone burns incense or sacrifices or offers a sacrificial meal or is bound to some sacred rites or priesthoods. That is like someone thinking adultery is to be counted only in kisses and embraces and in the actual union of flesh, or homicide only in the shedding of blood and the taking of a life.

But how much more widely the Lord arranges these things, we are certain, when he marks adultery even in desire, if someone fixes his eye lustfully and stirs his soul shamelessly (Matthew 5:28), when he judges homicide even in a word of cursing or insult and in every impulse of anger and in neglect of love for a brother (Matthew 5:22). So John teaches that whoever hates his brother is a murderer (1 John 3:15).

Otherwise the devil's cleverness in evil and God's lordship over discipline, by which he fortifies us against the expanses of the devil, would consist in very little, if we were judged only in those offenses which even the pagans have decreed must be punished. How will our righteousness abound beyond the scribes and Pharisees, as the Lord prescribed (Matthew 5:20), unless we have seen the abundance of its adversary, that is, of injustice? But if the head of injustice is idolatry, the first thing is that we be fortified in advance against the abundance of idolatry, while we recognize it not only in its open forms.
orientation: Tertullian is arguing that idolatry is the chief sin and must be understood in its full extent, not reduced to a few obvious acts.

title: The origin and scope of idol-making
english: There was a time when no idol existed. Before the craftsmen of this monster had arisen, temples stood empty and bare, and in some places the traces of that antiquity remain even today. Yet idolatry was already being practiced, not under that name, but in that deed. Even now it can be practiced outside a temple and without an idol.

But when the devil introduced into the world the craftsmen of statues and images and every kind of likeness, that rough business of human calamity took its name from idols and grew. From then on, every art that produces an idol in any way has become the head of idolatry.

It makes no difference whether a modeler shapes it, an engraver carves it, or an embroiderer weaves it, because the material does not matter either, whether the idol is formed from plaster, colors, stone, bronze, silver, or thread. Since idolatry can happen even without an idol, when an idol is present it makes no difference what kind it is, what material it is made of, or what likeness it bears. So no one should think that only something consecrated in human likeness is to be considered an idol.

For this, the interpretation of the word is necessary. Eidos in Greek means form; from it, by diminution, eidolon is derived. In the same way, among us forma produced formula. Therefore every form or formula demands to be called an idol. Hence idolatry is every service and servitude rendered to every idol. Hence every craftsman of an idol is guilty of one and the same crime, unless the people admitted idolatry too little because they consecrated for themselves the statue of a calf and not of a human being.
orientation: Tertullian is arguing that idolatry must be recognized beyond its open forms, and here he traces how the craft of making idols gave idolatry its name and made every maker of any idol guilty of the same crime.

title: God forbids both making and worshiping idols
english: God forbids an idol as much to be made as to be worshiped. Since the making comes first, so that what can be worshiped may exist, the prohibition of making comes first too, if worshiping is not allowed. For this reason—namely for eradicating the material of idolatry—the divine law proclaims: You shall not make an idol, and it adds, nor any likeness of the things that are in heaven, on earth, or in the sea (Exodus 20:4). By this it forbade the servants of God such arts throughout the whole world. Enoch had gone before, predicting that all the elements, all the wealth of the world—whatever is contained in heaven, in the sea, and on earth—would be turned into idolatry by the demons and spirits of the deserting angels, so that they might be consecrated against God in place of God. Human error therefore worships everything except the Creator of everything itself. Their images are idols; the consecration of images is idolatry. Whatever idolatry commits must be assigned to every craftsman and of whatever idol. In fact, the same Enoch condemns beforehand in his threat both the worshipers of the idol and its makers. And again Enoch says: I swear to you sinners, that sorrow is prepared for the day of blood and destruction—you who serve stones and who make images of gold, silver, wood, stone, and clay, and serve phantoms, demons, and spirits of the underworld and every error not according to knowledge; you will find no help from them. Isaiah indeed says: You are my witnesses, says the Lord: is there a God besides me? And they were nothing then, those who fashion and carve, all of them empty, who make for themselves what pleases them and will not profit them (Isaiah 44:9-10). And then follows that whole pronouncement in which he detests the craftsmen and the worshipers alike. Its closing words are: Know that their heart is ashes and earth, and no one can free his own soul (Isaiah 44:20). David likewise speaks of the makers: May those who make them become like them (Psalm 115:8). And why should I, a man of small memory, suggest anything further? Why should I recall more from the Scriptures? As if the voice of the Holy Spirit were not enough, or as if there were any need to deliberate whether the Lord has cursed and condemned the very craftsmen of those things whose worshipers he curses and condemns.
orientation: Tertullian is arguing that the divine law prohibits not only worshiping idols but also making them, and he quotes Enoch and Isaiah to show that craftsmen of idols are condemned along with their worshipers.

title: No excuse for idol-making crafts
english: I will answer the excuses of such craftsmen far more vigorously. If anyone knows that discipline, they should never be admitted into the house of God. The usual objection, "I have no other way to make a living," can be struck back more sharply: do you have to live, then? What do you have to do with God if you live by your own rules?

Then there is the argument they dare to draw from Scripture, that the apostle said each person should remain in the calling in which he was found (1 Corinthians 7:20). By that interpretation, all of us could continue in our sins. For none of us was found without sin, since Christ came down for no other reason than to set sinners free. They also say the same apostle commanded, following his own example, that each person should work with his own hands to earn a living (1 Thessalonians 4:11). If that command defends every kind of manual work, then I suppose pickpockets in the baths make their living with their hands, and robbers use their hands to do what they live by, and forgers certainly produce false documents not with their feet but with their hands, and actors earn their living not only with their hands but with their whole bodies. Let the church be open, then, to everyone who supports himself by his hands and his work, if no exception is made for the crafts that God's discipline does not accept.

But someone objects to the proposition that a likeness is forbidden: why, then, did Moses make a statue of a serpent out of bronze in the desert (Numbers 21:8-9)? Those figures were set apart. They were being prepared beforehand for a hidden purpose, not to relax the law, but to serve as patterns of their own meaning. Otherwise, if we interpret these things as opponents of the law do, should we too, like the Marcionites, attribute inconsistency to the Almighty? They destroy him in this way by making him changeable, since he forbids in one place and commands in another.

But if anyone fails to see that the figure of the bronze serpent hung up was designed to prefigure the Lord's cross, which would free us from serpents, that is, from the angels of the devil, while the serpent itself hung there as the devil slain, or whatever other explanation of that figure has been revealed to those more worthy, the apostle at least affirms that all these things happened to the people as figures (1 Corinthians 10:11). It is well that the same God both forbade the making of a likeness by the law and ordered the likeness of a serpent by an extraordinary command. If you obey the same God, you have his law: you shall not make a likeness (Exodus 20:4). But if you also look to the command for the likeness made afterward, then imitate Moses: do not make any statue contrary to the law, unless God has also commanded you.
orientation: Tertullian is answering excuses made by craftsmen who make idols, arguing that no one who knows Christian discipline may be admitted to God's house if they practice such arts.

title: Making idols is serving them
english: Suppose no law of God had forbidden us to make idols, and no voice of the Holy Spirit had threatened idol-makers no less than idol-worshippers. Even then, we could draw the conclusion from our very sacred commitment that arts of this kind are opposed to our faith. How have we renounced the devil and his angels if we make them? What divorce have we declared from them? I do not mean from those with whom we live, but from those by whom we live. What discord have we taken up against them, when for the sake of our display you acknowledge them? Do you destroy by word what you build by deed? Do you preach one God while you make so many? Do you preach the true God while you make false ones?

Someone says, "I make them, but I do not worship them." As if there were any reason he would not dare to worship them except the very reason he ought not to make them: the offense against God in both cases. No, you worship, because you make them so that they can be worshipped. And you worship not with the spirit of some cheapest vapor, but with your own spirit; not at the cost of an animal's life, but at the cost of your own soul. To them you sacrifice your talent; to them you pour out your sweat as a libation; to them you kindle your prudence. You are more to them than a priest, since through you they have a priest. Your diligence is their divinity. You deny that you worship what you make? But they do not deny it—the ones for whom you slaughter this fatter, more gilded, greater victim: your salvation all day long.
orientation: Tertullian is arguing that even making idols is forbidden, because it serves the demons Christians renounced at baptism.

title: The craftsman's hands defile the church
english: At this point the zeal of faith will plead with groans: a Christian comes from idols into the church, from the adversary's workshop into the house of God, and lifts up to God the Father hands that are mothers of idols. With those hands he worships, the very hands that outside are used to worship against God. He applies to the Lord's body the same hands that bestow bodies on demons. Nor is this enough. It would be a small thing if they only received from other hands what they defile, but they themselves hand on to others what they have defiled. Craftsmen of idols are chosen into the ecclesiastical order. O the crime! The Jews laid hands on Christ once; these men assault his body every day. O hands that ought to be cut off! Let them now consider whether it was said by way of comparison: if your hand causes you to stumble, cut it off (Matthew 5:30). Which hands more deserve to be cut off than those in which the Lord's body is caused to stumble?
orientation: Tertullian is denouncing idol-making craftsmen who come into the Christian assembly and handle the Lord's body with the same hands that serve idols.

title: Other crafts that serve idols without making them
english: There are also other kinds of crafts, and very many of them, which do not touch the making of idols, yet still supply the things without which idols can do nothing. They carry the same guilt. For it makes no difference whether you build or adorn, if you have constructed a temple, an altar, or a shrine for an idol, if you have embossed a thin plate of gold or its insignia, or even built a house. Work of this kind is greater, because it does not contribute the form but the authority.

If the necessity of making a living extends this far, there are other kinds of work that can provide support without deviation from discipline, that is, without fashioning an idol. The plasterer knows how to repair roofs and apply plaster, to line a cistern, to stretch cornices, and to curl many other ornaments onto walls besides statues. The painter, the marble worker, the bronze worker, and any engraver also know their own fields, and certainly much easier ones. For the one who draws a statue, how much more easily does he smear a sideboard? The one who carves Mars out of linden wood, how much more quickly does he put together a cabinet? No craft is not the mother or relative of another craft; nothing is without connection to something else. There are as many veins of crafts as there are desires of men.

But the difference lies in the wages and the price of the hands. The difference also lies in the labor. A smaller wage is repaid by more frequent work. How many walls desire statues? How many temples and houses are built for idols? But houses, palaces, baths, and apartment blocks, how many are there? The slipper and the sandal are gilded every day; Mercury and Serapis are not. Let that be enough for the profit of crafts. Luxury and ambition are more frequent than every superstition. Ambition will desire lances and cups more easily than superstition will. Luxury also spends more on crowns than solemnity does.

Therefore, when we urge people toward these kinds of crafts, which do not touch an idol or the things that belong to an idol, but which are often common to men and to idols, we must also beware of this: that nothing be requested from our hands by anyone, with our knowledge, for the service of idols. But if we allow it and do not act with the remedies already in use, I do not think we are free from the contagion of idolatry, we whose hands are caught not in ignorance but in the service, the honor, and the use of demons.
orientation: Tertullian is arguing that idolatry extends beyond making idols to every craft that supplies what idols need, and he is now listing trades that can be practiced without touching idolatry.

title: Astrology is a species of magic, condemned with it
english: We have noticed that among the trades there are also certain professions that are liable to idolatry. About astrologers one should not even speak. But since someone in recent days has provoked me by defending his persistence in that profession, I will say a few things.

I do not bring up the fact that he honors idols whose names he has written in the sky, to which he has assigned all the power of God, and that for this reason people do not think they need to seek God, since they presume that we are driven by the unchangeable will of the stars. I put forward one point: those angels were deserters of God, lovers of women, and betrayers also of this curiosity, and for that reason they were condemned by God. O divine sentence, reaching all the way to the earth with persistence, to which even those who do not know bear witness! Astrologers are expelled, just as their angels were. The city and Italy are forbidden to astrologers, just as heaven was forbidden to their angels. The same penalty of exile applies to disciples and masters.

But the magi and astrologers came from the East. We know that magic and astrology have fellowship with each other. So the first interpreters of the stars announced the birth of Christ; they were the first to give him gifts. By this, I suppose, they bound Christ to themselves. What then? Will the religion of those magi now serve as a defense for astrologers? Today, of course, astrology belongs to Christ: it observes and proclaims the stars of Christ, not of Saturn and Mars and every other dead thing of that order.

But, someone says, that knowledge was permitted until the gospel, so that once Christ was born no one from then on would interpret anyone's birth from the heavens. For they offered that frankincense and myrrh and gold to the infant Lord as a closing up, so to speak, of sacrifice and worldly glory, which Christ was going to take away.

What then did the dream suggest to those same magi, without doubt by God's will? That they should go to their own country, but by another way, not the way they had come. That is, they should not walk in their former sect. It was not that Herod should not pursue them, since he did not pursue them, being unaware that they had departed by another way, because he did not know the way they had come either. So we must understand the way as their sect and discipline. Therefore the magi were commanded to walk differently from then on.

So also that other kind of magic, which works through miracles, even when it rivaled Moses, drew out the patience of God until the gospel. For from then on even Simon Magus, already a believer, because he was still thinking something of his magic-trick sect, namely, to sell the Holy Spirit through the laying on of hands among the miracles of his profession, was cursed by the apostles and cast out of the faith. Another magus, who opposed the apostles along with Sergius Paulus, was punished with the loss of his eyes. I believe astrologers would have suffered the same if any had fallen in with the apostles. Nevertheless, since magic is punished, and astrology is a species of it, the species is certainly condemned in the genus.

After the gospel you will find nowhere any sophists or Chaldeans, by which I mean astrologers, or enchanters or diviners or magi, except plainly punished ones. Where is the wise man? Where is the scholar? Where is the debater of this age? Has not God made foolish the wisdom of this world? (1 Corinthians 1:20). You know nothing, astrologer, if you did not know you would become a Christian. If you did know, you should also have known this: that you would have nothing to do with that profession. The very art that foretells the critical periods of others' lives would have instructed you about its own danger. You have no part or lot in this matter. No one whose finger or rod abuses the heavens can hope for the kingdom of heaven.
orientation: Tertullian is arguing that certain professions are entangled with idolatry, and now turns to astrology, answering an objection that the magi who visited Christ legitimize the practice.

title: Schoolteachers and professors of literature are entangled in idolatry
english: We must also ask about schoolteachers and the other professors of literature. Indeed, there should be no doubt that they are close to idolatry in many ways. First, they must proclaim the gods of the nations, declare their names, genealogies, myths, and all their honorary trappings, and then observe the solemn festivals of those same gods, since their income is calculated from them. What schoolteacher will attend the Quinquatria without a tablet of the seven idols? He consecrates the very first fee of a new pupil to the honor and name of Minerva, so that even if he is not said to be defiled to any idol in word, he is still avoided as an idolater. What? Is there less pollution in this? Does a profit dedicated to an idol in its names and honors matter less than the Minervalia of Minerva, or the Saturnalia of Saturn, which even the little slaves must celebrate during the Saturnalia season? Yes, the strenae must be sought, and the Septimontium, and the Bruma, and the honorary gifts of dear kinship must all be exacted; the schools must be crowned for Flora; the flaminicae and the aediles offer sacrifices of created things; the school is honored with holidays. The same happens on an idol's birthday; every pomp of the devil is attended. Who will think these things are fitting for a Christian, unless he thinks they are fitting even for someone who is not a teacher? I know it can be said: if teaching literature is not permitted to God's servants, then learning it will not be permitted either. And how will anyone be trained in human wisdom for the time being, or in any understanding or activity, since literature is the instrument for all of life? How do we reject secular studies, without which divine studies cannot exist? Let us consider, then, the necessity of literary education. Let us recognize that it can partly not be admitted and partly be avoided. It is more fitting for believers to learn literature than to teach it. The principle of learning and teaching is different. If a believer teaches literature, he undoubtedly commends the praises of idols inserted in it while he teaches; he affirms them while he hands them down; he bears testimony to them while he mentions them. He seals the gods themselves with this name, since the law forbids, as we have said, the naming of gods and the placing of this name in vanity. From here the first faith in the devil is built from the beginnings of education. Ask whether someone who catechizes about idols commits idolatry. But when a believer learns these things, if he already knows what they are, he neither receives nor accepts them; much more so if he has known for a long time. Or when he begins to know, he should first know what he learned first, that is, about God and faith. Therefore he will reject those things and not receive them, and he will be as safe as one who knowingly receives poison from someone ignorant and does not drink it. For him necessity is counted as an excuse, because he cannot learn otherwise. But it is much easier not to teach literature than not to learn it, just as the rest of the school's defilements from public and private solemnities are easier for a believing pupil not to attend than for a teacher not to frequent.
orientation: Tertullian is arguing that Christians must avoid every profession connected with idolatry, and now turns from astrologers to schoolteachers and other teachers of literature.

title: Trade that serves idols is idolatry
english: Now let us consider the other kinds of wrongdoing that arise from trade. First, desire, the root of all evils, by which some have been entangled and have suffered shipwreck concerning the faith. Since the same apostle calls desire idolatry, and lying is desire's servant—I say nothing of perjury, since we are not even permitted to swear—is trade fitting for a servant of God? If desire departs, what reason is left for acquiring? When the reason for acquiring ceases, there will be no necessity for trading.

But suppose there is some just profit, free from the taint of desire and lying. I maintain that it still offends against idolatry, because it pertains to the very soul and spirit of idols and fattens every demon. Is that not idolatry in its primary form? Let them consider whether the same merchandise—I mean frankincense and other foreign goods used for idol sacrifice—is also useful to people for medicinal ointments, and to us as well for burial comforts. Certainly, when processions, priesthoods, and idol sacrifices are equipped through your dangers, losses, hardships, plans, errands, and trading, what else are you shown to be but a procurer of idols?

Let no one argue that this would make every kind of trade a matter of dispute. The graver the sin, the more diligently we must extend our watchfulness, so that we withdraw not only from the sins themselves but also from the means by which they are committed. Even if the act is done by others, it makes no difference if it is done through me. I must not be necessary to another when he does what is not permitted to me. From the fact that I am forbidden to do something, I should understand that I must take care that it not be done through me.

I observe this principle in another matter of no lighter guilt. Since I am forbidden from fornication, I provide no labor or complicity to others for that purpose. Since I have separated my own flesh from brothels, I recognize that I cannot practice pimping or any profit of that kind for another's sake. Likewise, the prohibition of homicide shows me that a trainer of gladiators is also barred from the church: he does not commit the act himself, but he supplies what another does.

Here is an even closer precedent. If a buyer of public victims comes to the faith, will you permit him to remain in that business? Or if he has already become a believer and undertakes it, will you think he should be retained in the church? I do not think so, unless someone will also overlook the frankincense dealer. Of course, the procurement of blood reaches some, and the procurement of fragrances reaches others.

If, before idols existed in the world, idolatry in its unformed state was carried on by these goods, and if even now the work of idolatry is nearly accomplished without an idol through the burning of fragrances, what greater service does the frankincense dealer render to demons? For idolatry is easier without an idol than without the frankincense dealer's merchandise.

Let us question the conscience of his faith itself. With what face will a Christian frankincense dealer pass through temples? With what face will he spit upon and blow upon the smoking altars for which he himself has provided? With what steadfastness will he exorcise his own nurslings, to whom he offers his house as a storehouse? If he casts out a demon, let him not congratulate himself on his faith. He has not cast out an enemy. He should easily obtain victory over the one he feeds daily.
Therefore no art, no profession, no trade that supplies anything for the equipping or forming of idols will be able to escape the charge of idolatry.
orientation: Tertullian is arguing that Christians must avoid every trade that supplies idol worship, now turning from schoolteachers to merchants and dealers in sacrificial goods.

title: No excuse of poverty or family can justify contact with idolatry
english: Unless, of course, we are to interpret idolatry as something other than the service of idols that are to be worshipped.

We flatter ourselves badly about the necessities of human livelihood if, after the faith has been sealed, we say, “I have no means to live.” Here I will answer that abrupt proposition more fully. It is said too late. It should have been deliberated beforehand, like that most provident builder who first reckons the costs of the work against his strength, so that when he has begun he will not later blush at his failure (Luke 14:28-30). But even now you have the Lord’s words and examples to take away every excuse from you. What do you say? “I will be in need.” But the Lord calls the poor blessed (Matthew 5:3). “I will have no food.” But he says, “Do not worry about your life, what you will eat” (Matthew 6:25). And for clothing we have the example of the lilies (Matthew 6:28). “I needed property.” But sell what you have and give to the poor (Matthew 19:21). “But I must provide for children and posterity.” No one who puts his hand to the plow and looks back is fit for the work (Luke 9:62). “But I was making conditions.” No one can serve two masters (Matthew 6:24). If you wish to be the Lord’s disciple, you must take up your cross and follow the Lord (Matthew 16:24)—that is, your hardships and torments, or your body alone, which is shaped like a cross. Parents, spouses, children will have to be left behind for God’s sake (Matthew 19:29). Do you hesitate about arts and trades and professions even for the sake of children and parents? It was shown to us already then that both pledges and crafts and businesses must be abandoned for the Lord’s sake, when James and John, called by the Lord, leave behind both their father and their boat (Matthew 4:21-22), when Matthew is roused from the tax booth (Matthew 9:9), when even burying a father was too slow for faith (Matthew 8:21-22). None of those whom the Lord chose said, “I have no means to live.” Faith does not fear hunger. It knows that hunger must be despised for God’s sake no less than every kind of death. It has learned not to look back at life—how much more at food? How few have fulfilled these things? But what is difficult among men is easy with God (Matthew 19:26).

Still, let us not flatter ourselves about God’s gentleness and mercy to the point of granting our necessities free rein all the way to associations with idolatry. Rather, let us avoid every breath of it, as if it were a plague, even from a distance—not only in the things we have already mentioned, but in the whole series of human superstition, whether it is devoted to their gods, to the dead, or to kings, as belonging to the same unclean spirits, now through sacrifices and priesthoods, now through spectacles and things of that kind, now through festival days.
orientation: Tertullian is answering Christians who, after being baptized, claim they must keep trades connected with idols because they have no other way to live.

title: Christians must not share pagan festive days
english: But why should I speak of sacrifices and priesthoods? I have already filled a volume on spectacles and pleasures of that kind. At this point I must return to the question of feast days and other extraordinary solemnities, which we sometimes subscribe to out of self-indulgence, sometimes out of timidity, sharing with the pagans in idolatrous matters against faith and discipline.

On this point I will first settle whether a servant of God ought to share with the pagans themselves in such things, whether in dress or in food or in any other kind of their rejoicing. "Rejoice with those who rejoice and mourn with those who mourn" was said by the apostle about brothers, urging unity of mind (Romans 12:15). But for these things there is no fellowship between light and darkness, life and death, or we tear apart what is written: "The world will rejoice, but you will mourn" (John 16:20). If we rejoice with the world, we must fear that we will also mourn with the world. But while the world rejoices, let us mourn, and when the world later mourns, we will rejoice.

So also Eleazar in the underworld received refreshment in Abraham's bosom, while the rich man was placed in the torment of fire, and they repay the alternating turns of evils and goods with rival retribution (Luke 16:23-25).

There are certain days of gifts, which among some discharge a title of honor, among others a debt of payment. "Now then," you say, "I will receive what is mine or repay what belongs to another." If people have consecrated this custom to themselves out of superstition, why do you, a stranger to all their vanity, participate in solemnities of things offered to idols, as though a day had been prescribed for you too, so that you cannot pay what you owe to a person or receive what is owed to you by a person without observing the day? Set your own terms for how you wish to be treated.

For why do you hide, when by another's ignorance you contaminate your own conscience? If you are not known to be a Christian, you are tempted and you act against another's conscience as though you were not a Christian; but if you have concealed it, you have been tempted and condemned. Certainly, whether this way or that, you are guilty of confusion in God. "Whoever is ashamed of me before men, I will also be ashamed of him," he says, "before my Father who is in heaven" (Matthew 10:33).
orientation: Tertullian is arguing that a servant of God must not join pagans in their festive days and celebrations, because these are idolatrous.

title: True blasphemy is abandoning Christian discipline, not being hated for it
english: But many have already persuaded themselves that it should be forgiven if at any time they do what pagans do, so that the name may not be blasphemed. Now the blasphemy which we must avoid in every way is, I think, this: if one of us leads a pagan to a just blasphemy by fraud or injury or insult or any other ground for legitimate complaint, in which the name is deservedly struck, so that the Lord too is deservedly angry. But if it was said of every blasphemy, 'Because of you my name is blasphemed' (Romans 2:24, citing Isaiah 52:5), we all perish, since the whole circus with its wicked acclamations attacks the name with no merit on our part. Let us stop, and it will not be blasphemed. No, let it be blasphemed, as long as we are in observance, not in deviation from discipline; as long as we are approved, not reproved. O blasphemy bordering on martyrdom, which testifies that I am a Christian at the very moment it detests me for that reason! The curse of the name is a blessing when discipline is kept.

'If I wanted to please men,' he says, 'I would not be a servant of Christ' (Galatians 1:10). But the same apostle elsewhere commands that we take care to please everyone. 'Just as I,' he says, 'please everyone in everything' (1 Corinthians 10:33). Surely he pleased men by celebrating the Saturnalia and the Kalends of January? Or by modesty and patience? By seriousness, by kindness, by integrity? Likewise when he says, 'I have become all things to all people, so that I might gain all' (1 Corinthians 9:22), was he an idolater to idolaters? A pagan to pagans? A worldly man to worldly people? But even if he does not forbid us to associate with idolaters and adulterers and other criminals, saying, 'Otherwise you would have to go out of the world' (1 Corinthians 5:10), he certainly does not let loose the reins of association to such an extent that, since it is necessary for us both to live with and mingle with sinners, we may also sin together with them. Where there is the commerce of life, which the apostle allows, there sinning together is what no one permits. It is permitted to live with pagans; it is not permitted to die with them. Let us live with everyone; let us rejoice together from the fellowship of nature, not of superstition. We are equal in soul, not in discipline; co-possessors of the world, not of error. But if we have no right of fellowship in such things with outsiders, how much more wicked is it to frequent these things among brothers. Who can endure or defend this?

The Holy Spirit reproaches the Jews for their festival days. 'Your sabbaths,' he says, 'and new moons and ceremonies my soul hates' (Isaiah 1:13-14). But we, to whom sabbaths are foreign, and new moons and festivals once loved by God, frequent the Saturnalia and the Kalends of January and the winter solstice and the Matronalia; gifts come and go, New Year's presents, games resound, banquets make a din. The faith of the pagans in their own sect is better, which claims no solemnity of the Christians for itself! They would not share with us the Lord's day or Pentecost, even if they knew them; for they would fear to seem Christians. We do not fear being pronounced pagans. If something must be indulged to the flesh, you have—I will not say only your own days—but more. For pagans each festival day comes once a year; for you every eighth day. Pick out each solemnity of the pagans and arrange them in order: they will not be able to fill up Pentecost.
orientation: Tertullian is answering Christians who think they may join pagan customs to avoid bringing the Christian name into disrepute.

title: Lamps and laurels at the doors
english: But, someone says, "Let your works shine" (Matthew 5:16). At present, it is our shops and doors that shine. You can now find more pagan doors without lamps and laurels than Christian ones. What should we think of this practice too? If it is honor of an idol, then without doubt honor of an idol is idolatry. If it is done for a person's sake, let us remember that all idolatry is done for a person's sake. Let us remember that all idolatry is worship offered to human beings, since even their own records show that the gods of the pagans were once human. So it makes no difference whether this superstition is offered to men of an earlier age or of this one. Idolatry is condemned not because of the persons who are put forward, but because of the services themselves, which belong to demons. "Render to Caesar the things that are Caesar's" (Matthew 22:21). It is good that he added, "and to God the things that are God's." What then are Caesar's? Clearly the matter under discussion at that time: whether the tax should be paid to Caesar or not. That is why the Lord asked for a coin to be shown to him and inquired whose image it bore. When he heard that it was Caesar's, he said, "Render to Caesar the things that are Caesar's, and to God the things that are God's" (Matthew 22:21)—that is, Caesar's image to Caesar, which is on the coin, and God's image to God, which is in the human being. So give your money to Caesar, but give yourself to God. Otherwise, what will belong to God if everything belongs to Caesar?

So, you say, are lamps before the doors and laurels on the doorposts an honor to God? Not at all, because what is honored is not God but the one who is honored in God's place by such services—as far as what is visible goes, while the working that is hidden reaches the demons. For we should be certain, if anyone is unaware through ignorance of secular literature, that the Romans even have gods of doorways: Cardea, named from hinges, and Forculus from doors, and Limentinus from the threshold, and Janus himself from the door. And we certainly know that although these names are empty and invented, when they are brought into superstition they draw demons to themselves, and every unclean spirit, through the bond of consecration. Otherwise demons have no individual names, but they find a name wherever they find a pledge. Among the Greeks too we read that Apollo Thyraeus and the Antelii are demons who guard doors. The Holy Spirit foresaw from the beginning that even doors would come into superstition, and foretold this through the most ancient prophet Enoch. For we see that other doors in the baths are also worshipped. But if there are beings worshipped at doors, then lamps and laurels belong to them. Whatever you do to a door, you have done to an idol.

At this point I call on God's authority as my witness, because it is not safe to suppress anything that has been shown to one person for the sake of all. I know a brother who was severely rebuked in a vision that same night because his servants had crowned his door when public rejoicings were suddenly announced. And yet he had not crowned it himself or ordered it; he had gone out earlier and on his return had rebuked what was done. So much are we judged before God in such matters even by the discipline of our household. Therefore, as far as honors to kings or emperors are concerned, we have enough instruction: we must be subject to magistrates and rulers and authorities in all obedience, according to the apostle's command, but within the limits of the discipline, as long as we are kept separate from idolatry. For that reason the example of the three brothers came first, who in other matters were obedient to King Nebuchadnezzar but most steadfastly refused to honor his image, proving that whatever is raised beyond the measure of human honor to the likeness of divine majesty is idolatry. So also Daniel, loyal to Darius in everything else, remained in office as long as he was free from danger to the discipline. For to avoid that danger, he feared the royal lions no more than the brothers feared the royal fires.

So let them light their lamps daily—lamps that have no light. Let them fasten laurels to their doorposts, laurels that will soon burn, with fires hanging over them. To them belong both the testimonies of darkness and the omens of punishment. You are the light of the world and a tree always green (Matthew 5:14). If you have renounced temples, do not make your door a temple. I have said too little: if you have renounced brothels, do not clothe your house with the face of a new brothel.
orientation: Tertullian is addressing Christians who decorate their doors with lamps and laurels for public festivals, and he is arguing that even these door-honors belong to idolatry.

title: Private and common ceremonies: when attendance is safe
english: Now consider the duties attached to private and common ceremonies: the toga of manhood, betrothals, weddings, name-days. I think there is no danger to be feared from the breath of idolatry that touches them. For we must consider the reasons for which the duty is performed. These I consider clean in themselves, because neither a man's dress nor a ring nor the union of marriage derives from the honor of any idol. In fact, I find no dress cursed by God except a woman's dress on a man. For it says, "Cursed is everyone who wears women's clothing" (Deuteronomy 22:5). The toga, however, is even called by a man's name. God no more forbids celebrating weddings than he does giving a name. But sacrifices are attached to these occasions. If I am invited, let the occasion not be titled as a sacrifice, and let the discharge of my service be as much as I choose. I wish indeed that we could not even see what we are forbidden to do. But since the evil one has surrounded the world with idolatry, it will be permitted to be present at certain things that hold us as dutiful to a person, not to an idol. If I am invited to a priesthood or a sacrifice, I will not go, for that is the proper duty of an idol. But neither will I serve in such a thing by counsel, by expense, or by any other work. If I am invited for the sake of a sacrifice and I attend, I will be a partaker of idolatry; if another reason joins me to the one sacrificing, I will be only a spectator of the sacrifice.
orientation: Tertullian is now applying his rule about idolatry to private and common social ceremonies, distinguishing the ceremony itself from the sacrifices attached to it.

title: Can a servant of God hold office without idolatry?
english: But what will faithful slaves or freedmen do? What will attendants do, who must stay close to their masters, patrons, or governors when those men offer sacrifice? If someone hands the unmixed wine to the one sacrificing, or even speaks a word that is necessary for the sacrifice, he will be considered a minister of idolatry. Keeping this rule in mind, we can still render service to magistrates and authorities, following the patriarchs and other ancestors, who served idolatrous kings right up to the limit of idolatry.

From this a debate has recently arisen: whether a servant of God may take on the administration of some dignity or power, if by some favor or cleverness he can keep himself untouched by every form of idolatry. After all, Joseph and Daniel were clean from idolatry and yet administered dignity and power in the adornment and purple of the prefecture of all Egypt or Babylon.

Let us grant, then, that someone can succeed in holding some honor and walk in the name of honor alone. He does not sacrifice. He does not lend his authority to sacrifices. He does not let out victims. He does not delegate the care of temples. He does not manage their revenues. He does not put on spectacles at his own or public expense or preside over putting them on. He pronounces or proclaims nothing solemn, and he does not even swear.

But as for the things that belong to power: he may not judge anyone's life or chastity, though you may judge about money. He may not condemn or prejudge. He may not bind anyone, nor imprison or torture anyone. If all this is believable as possible.
orientation: Tertullian is arguing that Christians must avoid every contact with idolatry, and now asks whether a Christian can hold public office if he avoids all idolatrous acts.

title: The trappings of honor are idolatrous
english: Now I must deal with the mere seat and display of honor. Each person has a distinctive dress, both for daily use and for honor and dignity. So that purple and the gold ornament for the neck were marks of dignity among the Egyptians and Babylonians in the same way that bordered togas, ceremonial robes, palm-embroidered robes, and golden crowns of provincial priests are now, but not under the same conditions. They were conferred only as a title of honor on those who deserved the friendship of kings. That is why they were called the purple-clad of the kings, from the purple, just as among us candidates are named from the white toga, but not so that this seat of office also bound them to priesthoods or any offices of idols. For if that had been so, men of such holiness and steadfastness would certainly have refused the polluted garments at once, and it would have appeared at once that Daniel did not serve idols or worship Bel or the dragon, which appeared much later. So that purple was simple, and no longer a mark of dignity but of free birth among the barbarians. For just as Joseph, who had been a slave, and Daniel, who had changed his status through captivity, obtained citizenship in Babylon and Egypt through the dress of barbarian free birth, so among us too, if necessary, the bordered toga can be allowed to boys and the robe to girls, marks of birth, not power; of family, not honor; of rank, not superstition. But the purple and the other marks of dignities and powers, attached to dignity and power, have been dedicated to idolatry from the beginning and carry the stain of their profanation, especially since bordered togas, ceremonial robes, and broad-striped tunics are also put on the idols themselves, and bundles of rods and staffs are carried before them. And rightly so. For the demons are the magistrates of this age; they carry the insignia of one college, the rods and the purple. What will you gain, then, if you use the seat of office but do not administer its works? No one can appear clean in unclean things. If you put on a tunic that is defiled in itself, perhaps it cannot be defiled by you, but you cannot be clean through it. Now, you who argue from Joseph and Daniel, know that old and new conditions, rough and polished, begun and completed, servile and free are not always to be compared. For they were also in the condition of slaves. But you are no one's slave, except Christ's alone, who freed you even from the captivity of the world, so you ought to act according to the Lord's pattern. That Lord walked in humility and obscurity, with no fixed home: for the Son of Man, he says, has nowhere to lay his head (Matthew 8:20). He was plain in dress, for he would not have said, Look, those who are clothed in soft garments are in the houses of kings. Finally, he was without glory in face and appearance, as Isaiah had also declared (Isaiah 53:2). If he exercised no right of power even over his own, for whom he performed humble service; if he fled from being made king, though he knew his own kingdom, he gave the fullest pattern to his own by directing them away from every eminence and seat, whether of dignity or of power. For who would have used these things more than the Son of God? What rods and how great would have escorted him, what purple would have bloomed from his shoulders, what gold would have shone from his head, if he had not judged the glory of the world alien to himself and his own? Therefore what he did not want, he rejected; what he rejected, he condemned; what he condemned, he counted in the pomp of the devil. For he would not have condemned it unless it were not his own. And things that are not God's cannot belong to anyone but the devil. If you have renounced the devil's pomp, know that whatever you touch from it is idolatry. Let this also remind you that all the powers and dignities of this age are not only alien to God but hostile to him, because through them punishments have been devised against God's servants, and through them the penalties prepared for the impious are ignored. But your birth and your property are troublesome to you in opposing idolatry. Remedies for avoiding it cannot be lacking, since even if they were lacking, that one remedy remains by which you are made fortunate, not as a magistrate on earth, but in heaven.
orientation: Tertullian is arguing that even the outward dress and insignia of public office are contaminated by idolatry, using Joseph and Daniel as apparent counterexamples.

title: Military service cannot be joined with the faith
english: This chapter might also settle the question of military service, which stands between rank and power. But the question now is whether a believer can turn to military service, and whether the military can be admitted to the faith—even the booted service or any lower kind, where there is no necessity of sacrifices or capital judgments. The divine sacred commitment and the human one do not agree, nor the sign of Christ and the sign of the devil, nor the camp of light and the camp of darkness. One soul cannot be owed to two masters, to God and to Caesar (Matthew 22:21). Moses carried a rod, Aaron a buckle, John is girded with a strap, Joshua led a battle line, and the people waged war—if you want to play games. But how will he wage war, indeed how will he even serve in peace without a sword, which the Lord took away? For even if soldiers had come to John and received a form of observance, and even if a centurion had believed, the Lord afterwards unbuckled every soldier by disarming Peter (Matthew 26:52). No dress is permitted among us that is assigned to an unlawful act.
orientation: Tertullian has just said that the only remedy for the trouble of birth and property is to be fortunate in heaven, not as a magistrate on earth; now he turns to the question of military service.

title: Idolatry in words and oaths
english: But since the conduct of divine discipline is endangered not only by deeds but also by words—for as it is written, "Behold the man and his deeds," so also "by your mouth you will be justified"—we must remember that the assault of idolatry in words must also be guarded against, whether from the fault of habit or of timidity. The law forbids naming the gods of the pagans, not that we should never pronounce their names when our way of life forces us to speak them. For often one must say: "You have him in the temple of Aesculapius," or "I live on the street of Isis," or "He has been made a priest of Jupiter," and many other things of this kind, since names of this sort are even given to people. For I do not honor Saturn if I call him by his own name, any more than I honor Marcus if I call him Marcus. But it says: "Do not mention the name of other gods, nor let it be heard from your mouth" (Exodus 23:13). He commanded this so that we should not call them gods. For in the first part of the law he says, "You shall not take the name of the Lord your God in vain" (Exodus 20:7)—that is, for an idol. So whoever honors an idol with the name of God has fallen into idolatry. But if gods must be spoken of, something must be added to make clear that I do not call them gods. For Scripture also names gods, but adds "their own" or "of the nations," as David did when he named gods, saying, "But the gods of the pagans are demons" (Psalm 96:5; Psalm 95:5 in the Septuagint). But this has been built up more for what follows. As for the rest, it is a fault of habit to say "By Hercules" or "By Medius Fidius," with the ignorance of some who do not know that it is an oath by Hercules. What will swearing by those you have renounced be but a violation of faith with idolatry? For who does not honor those by whom he swears?
orientation: Tertullian is arguing that idolatry can be committed not only by deeds but also by words, including naming pagan gods and swearing by them.

title: Silence and cursing as idolatry
english: It is timidity when someone else binds you by an oath or some testimony sworn by his gods, and you keep quiet so as not to be found out. For by keeping quiet you equally confirm their majesty, since you will seem to be bound for their sake. What difference does it make whether you confirm the gods of the nations by naming them as gods or by hearing them named? Whether you swear by idols, or, when adjured by another, you acquiesce?

Why do we not recognize the cunning of Satan? When he cannot accomplish it through our own mouth, he works to bring idolatry into us through the ears by the mouth of his own people. Certainly, whoever he is, he binds you either in a friendly or a hostile encounter. If hostile, you are already called to battle, and you know you must fight. If friendly, how much more safely will you transfer your oath to the Lord, so that you may dissolve the obligation of the one through whom the evil one was seeking to attach you to the honor of idols, that is, to idolatry.

All patience of this kind is idolatry. You honor those to whom you have shown compliance when they imposed themselves on you. I know a man—may the Lord pardon him—who, when it was said to him publicly in a dispute, 'May Jupiter be angry with you,' answered, 'No, with you.' What else would a pagan have done, who believed Jupiter to be a god? Even if he had not hurled back the curse by the same god, nor by any god like Jupiter, he had confirmed Jupiter as a god, since by cursing back he showed that he had borne the curse undeservedly through him. For why would you be angry through one whom you know to be nothing? If you rage, you already confirm that he exists, and the profession of your fear will be idolatry. How much more, when you curse back by him, do you do the same honor to Jupiter as the one who provoked you?

But a believer in such cases ought to laugh, not rage—indeed, according to the command, not even to curse back by a god, but plainly to bless by God, so that you both destroy idols and proclaim God and fulfill the discipline.
orientation: Tertullian is warning that even passive acceptance of pagan oaths or curses honors idols, and he is about to give examples of how a Christian should respond.

title: Blessings by pagan gods are idolatry
english: In the same way, someone initiated into Christ will not put up with being blessed through the gods of the pagans. He will not always reject the unclean blessing, but will turn it to God and cleanse it for himself. To be blessed through the gods of the pagans is to be cursed through God.

If I give someone alms or do him any kindness, and he then invokes his gods or the guardian spirit of his colony to be favorable to me, my gift or my work will become an honor to idols, because he repays the favor of the blessing through them. Why should he not know that I did it for God's sake, so that God rather may be glorified and demons not be honored in what I did for God? If God sees that I did it for His sake, He equally sees that I did not want to show that I did it for His sake, and I have in some way made His command into a thing offered to idols.

Many say that no one ought to make himself known; but I think he ought not even to deny it. For whoever conceals himself in any matter, being held as a pagan, denies—and certainly every denial is idolatry, just as every idolatry is denial, whether in deeds or in words.
orientation: Tertullian is warning believers that receiving a blessing in the name of pagan gods is a form of idolatry, even when it comes as thanks for a good deed.

title: The written denial is as guilty as the spoken one
english: But there is a kind of case, in deed and in word, that is two-edged and dangerous on both sides. It flatters you, as if it were harmless in either respect, as if the deed is not seen because the word is not held against you. When we borrow money from pagans, bound by pledges, we give security in writing under oath and deny ourselves. The pagans, of course, want to know the time of persecution, the place of the tribunal, and the person of the governor. Christ prescribes that one must not swear. "I wrote," someone says, "but I said nothing. The tongue, not the letter, kills."

Here I call on nature and conscience. Nature, because the hand can write nothing, even if the tongue rests motionless and quiet while dictating, that the soul has not dictated. Though the soul has dictated to the tongue itself, either something conceived by itself or handed over by another. Now, lest someone say, "Another dictated it," here I appeal to conscience: whether the soul accepts what another dictated and transmits it to the hand, whether the tongue accompanies it or rests. And rightly did the Lord say that sin is committed in the mind and conscience. "If desire or malice has ascended into the heart of a man," He says, "you are held as for the deed."

You have therefore given security for what has plainly ascended into your heart, which you cannot claim either not to have known or not to have willed. For when you gave security, you knew. When you knew, you certainly willed it. And it holds both as deed and as thought. Nor can you exclude the greater charge by a lesser one, saying that what you do not do is plainly made false by giving security. "Still, I did not deny, because I did not swear." On the contrary, even if you had done nothing of the sort, you would still be said to swear falsely if you consented to having done it. A voice silent in the pen still speaks, and a sound mute in letters still sounds.

But Zechariah, punished with temporary loss of voice, conversed with his mind while his tongue was useless. He dictated with his own hands from his heart and announced his son's name without his mouth (Luke 1:63). He speaks in the pen, he is heard in the wax, a hand clearer than any sound, a letter more vocal than any mouth. Ask whether he spoke who has been found to have spoken.

Let us pray the Lord that no necessity of this kind of contract surrounds us, and if it should happen, that He grant our brothers the means to work, or grant us the steadfastness to break off every necessity, so that those denying letters, substitutes for our mouth, may not be brought out against us on the day of judgment, sealed with signs no longer of accusers but of angels.
orientation: Tertullian is arguing that even a written denial of faith, such as a Christian signing a pledge when borrowing money from pagans, is a real denial and therefore idolatry.

title: The ship of faith amid idolatry's reefs, and the ark's exclusion of idolaters
english: Among these rocks and bays, among these shallows and straits of idolatry, faith sails with the Spirit of God as its wind. It is safe if it is careful, secure if it is watchful. But for those who are thrown overboard, the deep cannot be crossed by swimming. For those who are driven onto the rocks, the shipwreck cannot be escaped. For those who are swallowed down, the drowning in idolatry leaves no breath. Every wave of idolatry chokes those it overwhelms, and every whirlpool of idolatry sucks them down to the underworld.

Let no one say, "Who can be on guard so carefully? We would have to leave the world." As if leaving the world were not worth as much as standing in the world as an idolater. Nothing can be easier than guarding against idolatry, if the fear of it stands first in the mind. Any necessity is small when compared with so great a danger. For this reason the Holy Spirit, when the apostles consulted Him at that time, loosened the bond and yoke for us, so that we might be free to devote ourselves to avoiding idolatry.

This will be our law. The more unencumbered it is, the more fully it must be administered. It is the law proper to Christians, by which we are recognized and tested among pagans. This law must be set before those who are coming to the faith and pressed upon those who are entering the faith, so that those who come may deliberate, those who observe it may persevere, and those who do not observe it may renounce themselves.

For we shall see whether, according to the type of the ark, the raven and the kite and the wolf and the dog and the serpent will be in the church. Certainly the idolater is not found in the type of the ark. No animal was figured as an idolater. What was not in the ark should not be in the church.
orientation: Tertullian is concluding the treatise by picturing the Christian's perilous course through idolatry and then applying the type of Noah's ark to the church.
